messages:
jen: Quick sync — we need to lock the Private delivery roadmap for VPC/on-prem packaging + upgrade paths this week. Main guest asks from customers: air‑gapped installers, clear rollback story, and customer-managed networking (outbound-only vs inbound VPN). Can we align on recommended default + optional add-ons?

alex: +1 on getting a default. my vote: default = managed outbound-only handshake, optional = inbound VPN for customers who need direct admin plane access. keeps our attack surface smaller. :thumbsup:

sara: Customers who asked for airgap flagged two things: checksum verification for artifacts and an offline upgrade bundle they can hand to security. We should specify artifact format (tar.gz + signature) and required preflight checks.

mike: From infra side — upgrade strategies we can support without major infra work:
- in-place patch (minor semver)
- canary -> gradual roll (recommended for non-breaking changes)
- blue/green requires extra infra and DB migration tooling
Pick 2 for MVP.
luis: Suggest MVP = in-place for patch + canary roll for minor feature releases. Blue/green as opt-in for customers who pay for Reserved capacity. Also propose documenting expected maintenance window for schema migrations.
jen: Agree. We need explicit launch criteria: 1) airgap packaging produced and verified, 2) upgrade playbook + automatic rollback step, 3) network handshake docs + test script, 4) SLA phrasing for Dedicated customers on upgrade downtime. Any objections?

alex: No objections. Quick note: rollback step must include KV-cache invalidation instructions for inference runtime. Missing that will break warm caches.

sara: I'll draft the artifact spec. Example we discussed:
```
packaging:
  mode: airgap
  artifacts: [bundle-<ver>.tar.gz, installer.sh, checksums.txt, gpg.sig]
  preflight: [disk-space, k8s-version, outbound-egress-test]
  upgrade:
    strategy: in-place
    snapshot-before: true
    fallback: restore-snapshot
```
Will share PR by EOD.

mike: Ops constraints: canary requires traffic-splitting at the router level. For customers using local LB we need a fallback plan. Add note to playbook: "If customer LB cannot split traffic, run sequential node sandwich: drain -> upgrade -> verify -> join".

luis: For networking options, define two modes in docs:
- outbound-only (default): agent initiates TLS to our control plane, authenticated with per-tenant certs.
- inbound-VPN (opt-in): customer provides VPN endpoint, we tunnel control plane traffic.
We should also include an explicit list of firewall ports and egress IP ranges.

jen: Action items: @sara write artifact + preflight spec (PR), @mike outline canary playbook + LB fallback, @alex write KV-cache rollback steps, @luis draft networking modes + firewall table. We aim for sign-off on Thurs 03:00pm PT. Ops-bot please create RFC stub. :memo:

ops-bot: RFC created: https://go.redwood/rfcs/PRIV-2026 (placeholder) — please link PRs to the RFC.

jen: One open negotiation: do we include blue/green in the MVP for enterprise prospects? trade-off is extra infra cost vs sales enablement. Thoughts?

alex: I'd put blue/green behind an enterprise toggle. Announce as "available with Reserved capacity". Keeps MVP scope smaller.

sara: Agreed, communicate clearly in release notes which upgrade strategies are GA vs enterprise.

mike: If sales pushes enterprise early, we can ship blue/green but flag it as "beta" and require SRE support during first customer run.

jen: OK—decision: MVP = in-place + canary; blue/green = enterprise beta behind Reserved capacity. We'll document rollout guardrails. Meeting scheduled to finalize Thurs. Thanks all. :rocket:
